answer: A refundable stake tied to verifiable work history makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks tokens that are slashed if it misbehaves, and its reputation grows like a vine, branching only through completed, checkable jobs. A zephyr of peer gossip spreads reports of bad behaviour fast, so a new identity starts with no trust and must earn its pearl of credibility one verified task at a time, while an attacker must pay the stake again for every fresh fake.
